SPECIMEN

Diagnosis: Lung carcinoma
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Received Date: [redacted date]

TEST PERFORMED
ROS1 Gene Rearrangement Analysis by Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH)

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue sections using the Vysis LSI ROS1 (6q22) Dual Color Break Apart Rearrangement Probe (Abbott Molecular). H&E stained sections were reviewed to identify tumor areas. A total of 50 tumor cell nuclei were analyzed.

RESULT
ROS1 (6q22) rearrangement: NOT DETECTED

FISH analysis revealed 2-3 intact ROS1 signals per nucleus in the majority of cells examined. No evidence of ROS1 gene rearrangement was identified. The presence of 2-3 copies of ROS1 is of uncertain significance and may represent low-level polysomy of chromosome 6 or focal amplification.

INTERPRETATION
This patient's lung carcinoma is negative for ROS1 gene rearrangement. Based on this result, the patient is unlikely to benefit from ROS1-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as crizotinib, entrectinib, or lorlatinib.

The clinical significance of 2-3 copies of intact ROS1 remains uncertain and does not predict response to ROS1-targeted therapy.

Reported by: [redacted name], MD
Board Certified in Molecular Genetic Pathology
Report Date: [redacted date]
